title: Reflection Previews Beam AI Coding Model, Optimized for Efficiency
key_facts: Reflection AI unveiled Beam, its first model for writing code and using software tools, on 5 Oct 2026; selected users get an early version and others can join a waitlist.
Reflection's scorecard gives Beam 80.1 on Terminal Bench v2.1 against 63.8 for Inkling from Thinking Machines Lab (a US rival), and 65.5 against 54.3 on SWE Bench Pro v1.
Against Z.ai's GLM-5.2, Beam is ahead on SWE Bench Pro v1 (65.5 to 62.1) and slightly behind on Terminal Bench v2.1 (80.1 to 81.0).

Reflection's own table lists Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 at 88.3 on Terminal Bench v2.1, ahead of Beam; Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash reports 84.3 with fewer active parameters, but under different test settings, so the figures are separate vendor results, not a controlled comparison.
Beam has 501 billion parameters in total, 23 billion active per token (mixture-of-experts design).
Reflection says Beam reaches advanced-reasoning scores comparable to GLM-5.2 using three to four times less inference compute.
Reflection promises Beam's weights under Apache 2.0 later in October, plus a technical report and safety evaluations; Beam is still in final adversarial safety testing.
Chief executive Misha Laskin told Semafor that Reflection sees demand from organizations unwilling or unable to use Chinese models.
quote_evidence: Reflection’s chief executive Misha Laskin told Semafor that Reflection sees demand from organizations unwilling or unable to use Chinese models.
Reflection promises Beam’s weights under Apache 2.0 later in October, alongside documentation and tools for running, evaluating and fine-tuning the model.

why_it_matters_hint: Reflection pitches Beam as a US-built model organizations can run themselves, but the scores are its own and the weights are still unpublished.
